scope: single controlled fixed path; no PlayWorld score or SOTA claim

memory.method: bounded early-view pose KV retrieval; diagnostic, not paper reproduction
memory.pose_source: commanded poses, not reconstructed realized poses
memory.key_storage: exact native post-RoPE keys; original temporal/spatial positions retained

caveat: Commanded camera closure does not prove realized closure. Endpoint image similarity cannot establish world memory if the realized route fails.

visual_judge.prompt: Evaluate two anonymized world-model videos independently and then compare. Each was given the same image and fixed camera path. Commands by one-second chunk: ['WAIT', 'RIGHT', 'RIGHT', 'RIGHT', 'WAIT', 'WAIT', 'WAIT', 'WAIT', 'WAIT', 'WAIT', 'WAIT', 'WAIT', 'LEFT', 'LEFT', 'LEFT', 'WAIT']. RIGHT and LEFT yaw 60 degrees per second; W moves forward. Commands are NOT proof that motion happened. Inspect actual frames. Assess whether each video realizes a turnaround and return to the starting viewpoint; whether persistent landmark identity, any sign text, geometry and spatial layout match on return; and whether there are sudden jumps, frozen motion or implausible transitions. Distinguish camera-control failures from forgetting. Do not reward a similar final building if reaching it required a reset. Do not invent unseen geometry. Return English JSON with keys A and B (each with realized_round_trip: yes|no|uncertain, starting_place_recovered: yes|no|uncertain, discontinuity: yes|no|uncertain, visual_evidence, failure_classification), preference: A|B|tie|neither, confidence: low|medium|high, and reasoning. This is a diagnostic comparison, not a benchmark score.

A.visual_evidence: Frames 0-9 are static on the 'Primemall' building with its triangular roof and diamond-clad facade. Frames 10-~39 show a smooth rightward pan to a second zigzag-roof building with garbled signage ('Drienmaell', 'Primeeon'), a pool and blue umbrellas. Frames ~40-120 are nearly static on the plaza and sunken cafe, consistent with WAIT. From ~121 a blurred leftward pan passes back through the zigzag building. By ~135-145 (detail frame 7) the original building reappears with a correct-looking 'Primemall' sign, triangular roof and facade layout, briefly reading 'Primeraall' along the way. Rotation then continues past that view, and a new orange diamond-clad block with a glass storefront enters on the left. This block was not in the start frame. Frames 150-158 hold on this close-up block and alley, not on the original framing.
A.failure_classification: The return yaw is realized and the original landmark is recalled with largely consistent identity and geometry mid-turn. However, the camera overshoots or drifts during the LEFT segment and the model invents new foreground geometry. The final view is not the starting viewpoint. This is mainly a camera-control and rotation-calibration failure with some hallucinated additions, not wholesale forgetting.

B.visual_evidence: Frames 0-~120 are effectively identical to A: the start building, the right pan to the zigzag building and plaza, then a long static hold. During the LEFT pan (~121-130), an orange building reappears, but its sign degrades to 'Pinemall' or 'Pirenmell' and umbrellas and tables crowd the foreground. From ~131 a large new glass building with a bright blue diamond-panel band and a 'Prim...' logo emerges on the left and takes over the frame. It does not exist in the start view. Frames ~145-158 end in an alley between a brown building and the blue-band building, with a planter strip and a zigzag-roof structure in the distance. Neither the triangular-roof Primemall facade nor its sign is visible at the end.
B.failure_classification: Leftward motion occurs, so the camera responds to commands. On return, however, the model replaces the remembered start scene with a newly invented building and layout. Text identity is also degraded. This is primarily a memory/forgetting failure (scene re-synthesis) rather than a pure control failure.

result.reasoning: The two videos are nearly identical through the outbound turn and the WAIT period, so the difference lies in the return. A briefly reconstructs the original Primemall facade, with its triangular roof, sign text and layout, before overshooting and adding a hallucinated orange block. Its final frame therefore does not match the start. B never cleanly recovers the original view: its sign text degrades, and an entirely new blue-band building replaces the starting landmark by the end. Neither video truly returns to the starting viewpoint, but A shows better persistent landmark memory. B's failure is more severe forgetting and hallucination. Neither shows hard cuts or frozen motion beyond the commanded WAIT holds.
